guidance.title: Validate structured input at the service boundary
guidance.reusable_pattern: Define an expected schema and bounds, reject malformed input predictably, and keep diagnostic context separate from user-visible output.

specialist_route.when_to_use: novel parser, ambiguous trust boundary, or repeated validation bypass

guidance.title: Authorize the requested resource and action, not only the signed-in identity
guidance.reusable_pattern: Evaluate the caller, requested action, target resource, and relevant relationship; deny when required authorization evidence is absent.

specialist_route.when_to_use: shared roles, delegated administration, or cross-domain policy

guidance.title: Separate user-safe error messages from internal diagnostic detail
guidance.reusable_pattern: Return stable user-facing error categories with a correlation identifier; retain diagnostic detail in access-controlled operational evidence.

specialist_route.when_to_use: unclear sensitive-data boundary or cross-service failure semantics

guidance.title: Legacy input sanitization note
guidance.reusable_pattern: Legacy note retained for migration history only.

guidance.title: Research delegation notes
guidance.reusable_pattern: Document delegation boundaries and resource ownership before implementation.

guidance.title: Troubleshooting error-message note
guidance.reusable_pattern: Use a correlation identifier when escalating diagnostics.

exercises.title: Student import gains a new partner-supplied CSV field
exercises.scenario: A fictional ESS import receives a new optional field from an external partner. Sample files vary in encoding, field length, and row shape. The team must decide how the boundary should behave before release.
exercises.practice_goal: Use reusable input-boundary guidance to define accepted structure, bounds, failure behavior, and support diagnostics.
discussion_questions: Where would you look for the current pattern?
What should be explicitly accepted or rejected?
What evidence would show the behavior was tested?
When would specialist input be useful?
exercises.unsafe_shortcut: Accept any row that can be parsed and rely on downstream code to cope with unexpected structure.
reasoning_anchors: prefer current guidance over superseded note
exercises.specialist_trigger: The parser or trust boundary is novel, or the team cannot determine which malformed cases must be rejected.

exercises.title: Research administrator can act for several projects
exercises.scenario: A fictional RIS feature adds delegated administration. A signed-in administrator may update some research projects but not others, and a shared API serves several project types.
exercises.practice_goal: Separate authentication from authorization and make the requested action/resource relationship explicit.
discussion_questions: Which facts should the authorization decision depend on?
Where is the reusable authorization pattern?
How would you test cross-project boundaries?
What ambiguity should trigger IAM/security consultation?
exercises.unsafe_shortcut: Treat possession of a broad administrator role as sufficient for every project resource.
reasoning_anchors: caller plus action plus target resource
deny when required evidence is absent
test permitted and non-permitted project boundaries
exercises.specialist_trigger: Delegation crosses organizational or policy domains, or existing role semantics do not express resource ownership clearly.

exercises.title: Identity synchronization fails on an external dependency
exercises.scenario: A fictional IAM synchronization job receives an unexpected dependency response. Operators need enough detail to investigate, while end users should receive a stable supportable message.
exercises.practice_goal: Apply reusable error-handling guidance that preserves diagnostics without exposing unnecessary internal detail.
discussion_questions: What belongs in the user-facing response versus operational evidence?
How should a support engineer correlate the two?
When should reliability/security specialists join the design?
exercises.unsafe_shortcut: Return raw dependency exceptions directly to the caller so support has maximum detail.
reasoning_anchors: diagnostic detail retained in controlled evidence
exercises.specialist_trigger: The team is unsure whether diagnostic content crosses a sensitive-data boundary or how failures propagate across services.
